title: CLAUDE.md

title: CLAUDE.md
text: whole package thin orchestration layer single cached DuckDB connection, using DuckDB’s httpfs + spatial extensions query Overture’s Parquet files place. Connection lifecycle (R/stage_conn.R): stage_conn() lazily creates DuckDB connection caches options("overturer_conn"), overtureR calls session share one connection unless user passes conn. strike_stage() closes . utils.R::config_extensions() ensures httpfs/spatial installed loaded connection (workaround known duckdb 1.1.3 bug). Query construction (R/open_curtain.R — main entry point): 1. Builds read_parquet(...) glob URL base_url (S3 release default, local directory — see record_overture), partitioned theme=.../type=.... 2. Spatial filtering two layers, built SQL string fragments: set_stage_boundary() narrows partition-level bbox columns (cheap), focus_spotlight() adds ST_Intersects predicate actual geometry, accepting bbox, sf/sfc object, table name, another dbplyr tbl_sql spatial_filter (dispatched via audition_data()’s class sniffing). sf filter uploaded via sf_as_dbplyr() rather pulled R. 3. Executes CREATE REPLACE VIEW|TABLE returns dplyr::tbl() wrapped as_overture(). 4. get_theme_from_type() (R/get_theme_from_type.R) maps dataset type (e.g. "building") Overture theme (e.g. "buildings") via static type_theme_map — required whenever type "*"/NULL. overture_call class (R/as_overture.R): tbl_sql/tbl_lazy subclass carrying overture_playbill attribute (type, theme). lets record_overture() reconstruct fresh open_curtain() call new base_url downloading, collect.overture_call dispatches . Collecting sf (R/collect.R): collect.overture_call() converts DuckDB-native GEOMETRY column WKB calling parent dbplyr/dplyr collect() method, wraps result sf::st_as_sf(). result drops overture_call class (’s now -memory sf object, lazy query). Local materialization (R/record_overture.R): re-serializes current lazy query’s geometry WKB, renders SQL (dbplyr::sql_render), runs DuckDB COPY ... ... (FORMAT PARQUET, PARTITION_BY (theme, type)), preserving Overture’s partition layout. Returns new overture_call pointed downloaded directory via open_curtain(base_url = output_dir). snapshot_overture() convenience wrapper defaulting tempdir() + overwrite = TRUE. sf ↔︎ DuckDB bridge (R/sf_as_dbplyr.R): registers -memory sf object DuckDB view without copying data twice — geometry goes WKT text first (*_init view), second view casts DuckDB’s GEOMETRY type. Used internally focus_spotlight(), usable directly ad hoc spatial joins local sf object Overture data.

title: Load Overture Datasets as dbplyr and sf-Ready Data Frames
text: record_overture function allows download Overture Maps data local directory, maintaining partition structure S3. useful offline analysis need work data repeatedly. ’s example:
code: library(overtureR) library(ggplot2) library(dplyr) library(rayshader)  # Define a bounding box for New York City broadway <- c(xmin = -73.9901, ymin = 40.755488, xmax = -73.98, ymax = 40.76206)  # Download building data for NYC to a local directory local_buildings <- open_curtain("building", broadway) |>    record_overture(output_dir = tempdir(), overwrite = TRUE)  # The downloaded data is returned as a `dbplyr` object, same as the original (but faster!) broadway_buildings <- local_buildings |>    filter(!is.na(height)) |>    mutate(height = round(height)) |>    collect()   p <- ggplot(broadway_buildings) +   geom_sf(aes(fill = height)) +   scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Oranges", direction = 1) +   # guides(fill = FALSE) +   labs(title = "Buildings on Broadway", caption = "Data: Overture Maps", fill = "")  # Convert to 3D and render plot_gg(   p,   multicore = TRUE,   width = 6, height = 5, scale = 250,   windowsize = c(1032, 860),   zoom = 0.55,    phi = 40, theta = 0,   solid = FALSE,   offset_edges = TRUE,   sunangle = 75 )  render_snapshot(clear=TRUE)
